name: Atom layer selection
purpose: Decide whether reusable headless behavior belongs in Atom, an existing native element, Brick, a higher composition layer, or the application before composing a primitive.
decisionOrder: Start from the semantic and interaction job, not the desired appearance.
Use an existing native element when it already provides the complete reusable behavior contract.
Use an Atom primitive when reusable semantics, state, focus, keyboard, pointer, touch, portal, positioning, or compound composition are required.
Use Brick instead when the consumer needs a finished visual component; ordinary Brick applications should not import Atom directly.
Keep product workflows, page layout, content, routing, persistence, and analytics in higher layers.

selection.note: Choose Link for ordinary navigation and Pressable only for custom interactive surfaces.
Compose Toolbar only when grouped controls require toolbar keyboard behavior.

selection.use: NavList, NavigationMenu, Breadcrumb, BottomNavigation, Tabs, or Pagination
selection.note: Select by the navigation relationship, not by visual resemblance.
Do not recreate dialog focus, dismissal, portal, or labeling behavior.

selection.intent: scrollable viewport with owned scrollbar behavior

selection.note: Use a native img when loading state and fallback composition are unnecessary.
Choose Collapsible for one independent disclosure and Tabs for one shared switching panel.
Choose NavList or an interactive collection primitive when items navigate, select, or activate.

rules.statement: Keep Atom guidance and compositions headless; do not add visual recipes, color, theme, product copy, or application layout policy.
Preserve native semantics and behavior unless Atom explicitly owns the added reusable contract.
Do not rebuild focus, keyboard, pointer, touch, portal, positioning, or controlled-state behavior already owned by an Atom primitive.
When building with Brick, consume Brick public components and let Brick consume Atom rather than importing both layers directly.

nativeFallback.check: Search Atom's manifest, public exports, and related component guides for the required behavior before using a native fallback.
nativeFallback.use: Use the narrowest semantic native element only when no Atom primitive owns the behavior and no reusable state or interaction contract is being recreated.
nativeFallback.report: Record the missing primitive or intentional native choice so repeated gaps can be evaluated by Atom maintainers.

validation: Name the selected semantic and interaction job and its owning layer.
Confirm no visual or application policy entered the Atom composition.
Confirm the rendered elements, accessible names, state, focus, keyboard, pointer, touch, and RTL behavior that apply.
Record any native fallback and the Atom capability searched first.
